title: Triage emails, leads and comments with a cautious agent
summary: A builder rebuilt their agent as a five-step pipeline that labels and scores incoming items; they report it quarantined phishing, booked a call and held an unsure comment for review.
agent_role: The model only labels and scores each incoming item; plain code carries out actions above a 0.85 confidence line, and anything below waits for the human.
outcome: Author reports about $0.38 per 10,000 decisions, a run costing $0.13 using 3 of 10 allowed actions, with a phishing email quarantined and a lead call booked.
what_they_did: The poster replaced one big do-everything prompt with five steps. Each incoming email, comment, lead or page is packed into a small summary card. The model answers a few short questions with labels and scores. Items scoring 0.85 or higher get handled by plain code; lower ones wait for the poster.
how_it_went: They report a phishing lookalike scored 0.97 and was quarantined, a lead scored 0.91 and got a call booked, and a comment at 0.71 was held for them. The run cost $0.13 against a $1 cap.
worth_knowing: The agent can never post anything public by itself; that rule is written into the code, not just asked of the model. The poster says to count retries and cleanup when judging cost.
prompt: Help me build a triage agent for my [email inbox / comments / sales leads]. For each new item, summarize it into a short card. Then answer small questions: which folder, worth replying yes or no, urgency from low to critical, each with a confidence score from 0 to 1. Only act when confidence is at least [0.85]; otherwise put it in a review list for me. Allowed actions: [move email, send calendar link, notify me]. Never post or send anything public without my approval. Cap each run at [10] actions and [$1] of spend. Show me the plan and a test run on [5] sample items before turning it on.

curation.rationale: A real triage agent with a clear design, a confidence cutoff that hands unsure cases to a human, and concrete cost numbers; evidence is a self-reported video run.
